title: SharePoint admin center: Data access governance report of sites a group can access
summary: The briefing accurately reports Microsoft's planned group-permissions report and distinguishes it from the documented user report. The rollout dates match Microsoft's notice, and the briefing appropriately leaves report-specific licensing, controls and limits unconfirmed.

claims.claim: The new SharePoint admin center Data access governance report identifies every site a given group can access.
claims.quote: We are introducing a new Data access governance report in the SharePoint admin center that allows SharePoint administrators to identify all sites accessible to a given group and the extent of that access.

claims.claim: The group report shows the extent of the group's access to the sites.
claims.quote: With this new report, SharePoint admins can now see every site a group can access and the extent of that access.

claims.claim: Broad-membership groups, including vendor groups, can expose sensitive content to unintended recipients.
claims.quote: A single group with broad membership or a special group for vendors etc. - can expose sensitive content to unintended recipients.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft's notice says rollout begins in late November 2026.
claims.quote: General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Rollout will begin in late November 2026 and is expected to complete by early December 2026.

claims.claim: Microsoft expects rollout to complete by early December 2026.
claims.quote: Rollout will begin in late November 2026 and is expected to complete by early December 2026.

claims.claim: The notice sets no act-by date.
claims.quote: Act by: none

claims.claim: The notice's end date is 2027-01-08.
claims.quote: Microsoft's end date 2027-01-08

claims.claim: Microsoft names SharePoint administrators responsible for managing and reviewing site permissions as the affected audience.
claims.quote:
Who is affected

- SharePoint administrators responsible for managing and reviewing site permissions.

claims.claim: Microsoft says administrators can use the report to investigate potential sensitive-content exposure.
claims.quote: Administrators can use the report to investigate potential exposure of sensitive content and to review group permissions before assigning Copilot licenses.

claims.claim: Microsoft names reviewing group permissions before assigning Copilot licences as a use of the report.
claims.quote: Administrators can use the report to investigate potential exposure of sensitive content and to review group permissions before assigning Copilot licenses.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends notifying SharePoint administrators about the new reporting capability.
claims.quote: Notify your SharePoint administrators about the new reporting capability in the SharePoint admin center.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends updating internal documentation and workflows.
claims.quote: Update your internal documentation and workflows to reflect this change.

claims.claim: Microsoft's notice places the new report on the Data access governance page.
claims.quote:
Platforms and services

- Microsoft SharePoint admin center- Data access governance

claims.claim: Learn does not yet describe this report for an arbitrarily selected group, including in its Data access governance overview.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint "given group" "report" licensing role default PowerShell; opened DAG overview, user report, prerequisites and PowerShell guide. Found user and fixed Everyone/EEEU reports, not the roadmap's given-group report.

claims.claim: The group report's default state is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint "given group" "report" "CSV" "48" "default"; SharePoint "group permissions report" licensing price default enabled administrator limits. Read MC1540348, DAG overview and PowerShell references; no group-report default stated.

claims.where: front matter: licensing; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Report-specific licensing is not yet published, so the licensing model is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint "group permissions" "Data access governance" report price meter enable; SharePoint "group" "Data access governance" "role" "license". Opened DAG overview, SAM prerequisites and Start reference; none names the given-group report entitlement.

claims.claim: No price is published for the given-group report.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint "group permissions" "Data access governance" report price meter enable; SharePoint "group permissions report" licensing price default enabled administrator limits. Opened DAG overview and SAM prerequisites; no given-group report price found.

claims.claim: No meter is published for the given-group report.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint "group permissions" "Data access governance" report price meter enable. Opened DAG overview, SAM prerequisites and PowerShell guide; no meter for the given-group report found.

claims.claim: Learn documents neither the exact UI procedure nor a PowerShell command or group-specific parameter set for the given-group report.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint "given group" "Data access governance" PowerShell Graph report admin center. Opened DAG overview, PowerShell guide, Start and Get references; only user and fixed Everyone/EEEU reporting found, not arbitrary-group inputs or a group parameter set.

claims.claim: The given-group report's output format is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint "given group" "report" "CSV" "48" "default". Opened DAG overview, user report and PowerShell guide; CSV instructions describe existing reports, not the given-group report.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not specify which administrative role the given-group report requires.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint "group" "report" "Data access governance" "role" "license". Opened SAM prerequisites, DAG overview and PowerShell guide; role requirements found for existing reports, not this report. MC1540348 names SharePoint administrators as its audience.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented whether the group report shares the user report's data-age, report-count or rerun limits.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint "group" "Data access governance" report "30 days" "five"; SharePoint "given group" "report" "CSV" "48" "default". Opened user report, DAG overview and PowerShell guide; no corresponding given-group limits found.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published whether the group report is classified as a snapshot report.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint data access governance group permissions report group licensing PowerShell default. Opened DAG overview's snapshot-report descriptions, SAM prerequisites and PowerShell guide; none classifies the given-group report.

claims.claim: The existing site permissions for users report lists all sites a specified user can access, rather than taking a group as its reporting subject.
claims.quote: This report lists all sites a user can access and helps admins determine whether they can access the entire site or specific sections, granted directly to the user or indirectly through groups.

claims.claim: The user report distinguishes access to the entire site from access to specific sections.
claims.quote: You can determine whether the entire site is shared with the user or only a few files or items are shared.

claims.claim: The user report covers direct access and access granted indirectly through groups.
claims.quote: This report lists all sites a user can access and helps admins determine whether they can access the entire site or specific sections, granted directly to the user or indirectly through groups.

claims.claim: The existing user report can be downloaded as CSV.
claims.quote: Select Download report for the selected user option to download the report as a CSV file.

claims.claim: Learn lists nonpseudonymized report data as a known issue that might stop Data access governance reports working.
claims.quote: Reports might not work if you select nonpseudonymized report data for your organization.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Changing the report-name concealment setting requires a Global Administrator.
claims.quote: To change this setting, you must be a Global Administrator.

claims.claim: Learn directs administrators to the Reports setting in the Microsoft 365 admin center and says to clear Display concealed user, group, and site names in all reports.
claims.quote: Go to the Reports setting in the Microsoft 365 admin center and clear Display concealed user, group, and site names in all reports.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn names Restricted access control as a follow-up remediation option for Data access governance findings.
claims.quote: Use Restricted access control (RAC) to limit access to a specific group.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn names the Change history report as a follow-up option to investigate permission changes.
claims.quote: Review the 'Change history' report to identify recent permission changes that might have led to oversharing.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn names Site access review as a follow-up option for site owners to review and update permissions.
claims.quote: Use the Site access review feature to request that site owners review and update permissions.

claims.claim: The SAM prerequisites page lists SharePoint Administrator as an administrative role.
claims.quote: SharePoint Administrator: Provides full administrative control over the SharePoint Online service, including sites, policies, groups, and operational tasks, such as service health and support.

claims.claim: SharePoint Advanced Management Administrator includes wider governance capabilities such as viewing metadata across SharePoint content.
claims.quote:
SharePoint Advanced Management Administrator: Includes all SharePoint Administrator capabilities, plus advanced governance capabilities such as:

- Viewing metadata (names, paths, URLs) across SharePoint content

claims.claim: The user report captures data from up to 48 hours before generation.
claims.quote: Reports capture data from up to 48 hours before generation.

claims.claim: The user report has a limit of five reports.
claims.quote: You can have up to five reports.

claims.claim: The user report can be rerun every 30 days.
claims.quote: You can run reports again every 30 days.

claims.claim: Microsoft says to generate the site permissions for your organization report at least once before creating the user report.
claims.quote: Make sure that the site permissions for your organization report is generated at least once.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The Data access governance overview refers readers to the SAM prerequisites for general report prerequisites.
claims.quote:
What you need to create a data access governance report

See Prerequisites for SharePoint Advanced Management.

claims.claim: At least one user assigned a Microsoft Copilot licence is a documented route to SAM capabilities supporting Copilot deployment.
claims.quote: At least one user in your organization is assigned a Microsoft Copilot license. (The user doesn't need to be a SharePoint administrator.)

claims.claim: SharePoint K, P1 or P2 combined with the SharePoint Advanced Management Plan 1 add-on is another documented SAM entitlement route.
claims.quote: Your subscription includes SharePoint K, P1, or P2, and your organization purchases the SharePoint Advanced Management Plan 1 add-on.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 E7 is a documented SAM entitlement route.
claims.quote: Your organization has Microsoft 365 E7, also known as The Frontier Suite.

claims.claim: The SAM prerequisites require a listed base subscription: Office 365 E3, E5 or A5; Microsoft 365 E1, E3, E5 or A5; or Microsoft 365 GCC, GCC-High or DoD.
claims.quote:
Your organization must have one of the following base licenses:

- Office 365 E3, E5, or A5
- Microsoft 365 E1, E3, E5, or A5
- Microsoft 365 GCC, GCC-High, or DoD

claims.claim: IT administrators with Microsoft 365 E5 licensing can access Data access governance reporting.
claims.quote: IT administrators with Microsoft 365 E5 licensing can access Data access governance reporting

claims.claim: The overview says that this E5 reporting entitlement does not allow viewing or using the other SAM features.
claims.quote: IT administrators with Microsoft 365 E5 licensing can access Data access governance reporting, but can't view or use the other SharePoint Advanced Management features.

claims.claim: The E5-only reporting entitlement excludes snapshot reports and remedial actions.
claims.quote: The reports don't provide snapshot reports or remedial actions.

claims.claim: Learn says Data access governance reports are currently unavailable for Microsoft 365 operated by 21Vianet even with the required licences.
claims.quote: The reports are currently unavailable for Microsoft 365 operated by 21Vianet, even if you have the required licenses.

claims.claim: The existing Data access governance landing page is reached in the SharePoint admin center through Reports > Data access governance.
claims.quote: In the left pane, expand Reports and then select Data access governance.

claims.claim: Get-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportEntity <entity> lists existing DAG reports using the SharePoint Online PowerShell module.
claims.quote:
Lists various 'Data Access Governance' (DAG) reports in SharePoint admin center.

Get-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight
    -ReportEntity <ReportEntityEnum>
    [-Workload <WorkloadEnum>]
    [-ReportType <ReportTypeEnum>]

claims.claim: The user report creation page is reached through Reports > Data access governance > Site permissions for users > View reports > Create report.
claims.quote:
From the Data access governance landing page, select View reports under Site permissions for users.
2. Select Create report to generate your report.

claims.claim: The user-report Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight call uses PermissionsReport, Snapshot, SharePoint, Name and UserPrincipalNames as shown, in Microsoft.Online.SharePoint.PowerShell.
claims.quote:
Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight
    -ReportEntity <ReportEntityEnum>
    -Workload <WorkloadEnum>
    -ReportType <ReportTypeEnum>
    -Name <String>
    -UserPrincipalNames <System.Collections.Generic.List`1[System.String]>

claims.claim: The PowerShell guide spells the user-report input parameter UserEmailList, whereas the cmdlet reference uses UserPrincipalNames.
claims.quote: Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportEntity PermissionsReport -ReportType Snapshot -Workload SharePoint -Name "UserSharePointReport" -UserEmailList "a@contoso.com","b@contoso.com"

claims.claim: The PowerShell guide says the user-report input values must be user principal names despite its UserEmailList parameter spelling.
claims.quote: While the parameter is named UserEmailList, the report requires user principal names.

claims.claim: The Start cmdlet's ReportEntity accepted values include PermissionsReport and PermissionedUsers.
claims.quote: Everyone, EveryoneExceptExternalUsers, EveryoneExceptExternalUsersAtSite, EveryoneExceptExternalUsersForItems, PermissionedUsers, PermissionsReport, SensitivityLabelForFiles, SharingLinks_Anyone, SharingLinks_Guests, SharingLinks_PeopleInYourOrg

claims.claim: Learn says to sign in to the SharePoint admin center with SharePoint administrator credentials to access Data access governance.
claims.quote: Sign in to the SharePoint admin center with the SharePoint administrator credentials for your organization.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Why it matters; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: Microsoft's notice describes an administrator-used report, not an automatic change to group permissions or an end-user workflow.
claims.quote: SharePoint administrators will be able to use the new report to identify all sites accessible to a given group. The report will show the extent of the group's access to those sites.
